Note::TexAccessor::strip_cites¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_cites() const

Remove Complete Citation Calls¶

strip_cites() removes complete citation-family calls whose control-word name begins with cite, including starred forms and variants such as \citep and \citet. Any number of balanced optional groups may precede the required braced key group. The whole call is removed; citation keys and notes are not left in the prose.

Matching is lexical and exact at the command boundary. Escaped commands and calls without a complete required group remain unchanged. Nested braces in the key group and brackets inside optional notes are balanced. Use citations when citation arguments should be extracted rather than discarded, and strip_bib for bibliography declarations and reference-list environments.

Whitespace is collapsed and trimmed after removal. The returned Text Note is a new, shape-preserving allocation; the receiver is unchanged. Undefined input remains undefined and non-Text dtypes reject. Work is linear in source bytes.

Example 1: Notes, Stars, Nested Keys, And Malformed Calls¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \citep[see][p.~2]{alpha,{beta}} B \cite*{gamma} C)",
    R"(\\cite{escaped} \cite{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_cites() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["A B C", "\\\\cite{escaped} \\cite{unfinished"]

Example 2: Variants Preserve A Matrix’s Structure¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(Lead \citet{a} tail)", R"(\citeauthor*{b})",
                             "uncited prose", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_cites();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_cites()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["Lead tail", ""], 
  ["uncited prose", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
idempotent=true

The lexical family rule includes \citet and \citeauthor*; a cell that contains only a citation becomes an empty string without changing matrix position.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_cites().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_cites();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip cites Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip cites Int64: rejected
